Within this whole period, when it is available, "in the waxing fortnight" (āpūryamāṇa-pakṣa), the bright fortnight; and within that too, when it is available, "on a puṇya-day" — i.e., on a day favourable to oneself, conducive to the success of the karma.

"For twelve days" — beginning from a puṇya-day prior to the day on which one wishes to perform the karma, for twelve days, "observing the upasad-vow." The vow pertaining to the upasads is well known in the jyotiṣṭoma; there it consists in subsisting on milk through the gradual increase and decrease of the breast-portion. Here, however, since that whole rite is not bodily transferred, only the bare drinking of milk — devoid of the accompanying procedure (itikartavyatā) — is taken up. If, however, one analyses the compound as "the vow of the upasads" (upasadāṃ vratam), then the entire procedural form ought to be included; why is that not adopted?

The answer: because this karma is smārta. For this mantha-karma is smārta in character. Objection: being prescribed by śruti, how can it be smārta? — for this śruti is merely an anuvāda of smṛti. If it were śrauta, there would be the relation of prakṛti and vikṛti; and consequently the vikṛti-karma would adopt the dharmas of the prakṛti. But there is no śrauta-character here; it is for this very reason that this karma is enjoined in the āvasathya fire, and the entire āvṛt is purely smārta.

"Having become one observing the upasad-vow" — i.e., subsisting on milk; "in an udumbara" — made of udumbara wood; "kaṃsa or camasa" — its qualifications: of the shape of a kaṃsa or of a camasa, but in either case of udumbara only. The option lies in the form, not in its being of udumbara.

Here "all-herb" (sarvauṣadham) means the collection of all herbs; one should gather all herbs as far as possible and according to one's capacity. Among the cultivated herbs, ten are obligatorily to be taken — rice, barley, etc., to be enumerated. Taking more is no fault. The fruits of cultivated plants likewise, as far as possible and according to capacity. The word "iti" indicates the totality of the materials to be collected; whatever else is to be gathered should all be gathered. The order is to be ascertained from the gṛhya-sūtras.

"Sweeping around and smearing" is the consecration of the ground. Since it is said "having installed the fire," it is understood that this is in the āvasathya fire — both because of the singular number and because of the mention of "installation"; for it is only the fire already existing that is "installed." "Having strewn" the kuśa-grass. "By the (standard) āvṛt" — since the karma is smārta, the sthālīpāka-procedure is to be adopted; by that, having consecrated the ghee.

"By a male nakṣatra" — a nakṣatra of masculine name, conjoined with the puṇya-day. "The mantha" — the paste of all herbs and fruits — having sprinkled it in the udumbara cup with curd, honey and ghee, having churned it together with a single churning-stick, "having brought it together" — i.e., placed in the middle — with an udumbara ladle, in the place of pouring, he offers oblations of ghee with these mantras, "yāvanto devāḥ" and the rest.
BR_C06_S03_V02::block-0: "To the eldest, svāhā; to the best, svāhā" — having offered thus into the fire, he pours the residue into the mantha. "To prāṇa, svāhā; to the most excellent (Vasiṣṭhā), svāhā" — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the mantha. "To speech, svāhā; to support, svāhā" — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the mantha. "To the eye, svāhā; to prosperity, svāhā" — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the mantha. "To the ear, svāhā; to abode, svāhā" — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the mantha. "To the mind, svāhā; to progeny, svāhā" — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the mantha. "To semen, svāhā" — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the mantha.
BR_C06_S03_V03::block-0: "To Agni, svāhā" — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the mantha. "To Soma, svāhā" — and likewise. "Bhūḥ, svāhā; bhuvaḥ, svāhā; svaḥ, svāhā; bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ, svāhā" — each followed by pouring the residue into the mantha. "To Brahman, svāhā; to Kṣatra, svāhā; to the past, svāhā; to the future, svāhā; to the universe, svāhā; to the all, svāhā; to Prajāpati, svāhā" — each in like manner offered into the fire and the residue poured into the mantha.
BR_C06_S03_V03::block-1:
Beginning with "to the eldest, svāhā; to the best, svāhā," having offered two oblations at a time, he pours the residue into the mantha — i.e., the ghee adhering to the ladle he causes to flow into the mantha. From this very mark of "eldest, best," etc. — these being characteristics of prāṇa — it follows that only one who knows the prāṇa as eldest, best and so on is qualified for this karma.

Beginning with "to semen," he offers one oblation at a time and pours the residue into the mantha. He then churns it again with another churning-stick.
BR_C06_S03_V04::block-0: Then he touches it (the mantha), saying: "Thou art moving, thou art blazing, thou art full, thou art firmly fixed, thou art the one common seat; thou art the hiṅkāra, thou art that which is hiṅkṛta; thou art the udgītha, thou art that which is being udgīta; thou art that which is announced, thou art that which is responded to; thou art kindled in the moist; thou art all-pervading, thou art powerful; thou art food, thou art light, thou art the end, thou art the absorber."
BR_C06_S03_V04::block-1: "Then he touches it" — namely with this mantra, "Thou art moving (bhramad-asi)."
BR_C06_S03_V05::block-0: Then he raises it up, saying: "Thou art Āma by name, for thine is all this; he indeed is the king, the lord, the over-ruler — may that king, lord, over-ruler make me king, lord, over-ruler."
BR_C06_S03_V05::block-1: "Then he raises it up" — i.e., he takes it up in his hand together with the vessel, with the mantra "Āmaṃ-syāmaṃ hi te mahi."
BR_C06_S03_V06::block-0: Then he sips it, saying: "That excellent (light) of Savitṛ — the winds are sweet for the righteous, sweet flow the rivers; may the herbs be full of sweetness for us. Bhūḥ, svāhā. May we meditate upon the splendour of the god — sweet is the night, sweet the dawns, sweet is the earthly dust; sweet may heaven, our father, be. Bhuvaḥ, svāhā. May he impel our intellects — sweet may the lord of the forest be for us, sweet may the sun be; sweet may the cows be for us. Svaḥ, svāhā." Then having recited the entire Sāvitrī and all the madhumatī verses, he says: "May I myself become all this — bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ, svāhā," and then sips. Having washed his hands, he lies down behind the fire with his head to the east. In the morning, he worships the sun with: "Of the directions thou art the one lotus; may I become the one lotus among men." Then, going back the same way, seated behind the fire, he recites the lineage (vaṃśa).
BR_C06_S03_V06::block-1:
"Then he sips (ācāmati) it" — i.e., consumes it. With the first quarter of the Gāyatrī and the first madhumatī verse and the first vyāhṛti, he takes the first mouthful; with the second quarter of the Gāyatrī, the second madhumatī verse, and the second vyāhṛti, the second mouthful; with the third quarter of the Gāyatrī, the third madhumatī verse, and the third vyāhṛti, the third mouthful.

Having recited the whole Sāvitrī and all the madhumatī verses, and at the end "May I myself become all this," with "bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ svāhā" he consumes it all together. One should so determine beforehand that the entire substance is exhausted in four mouthfuls. Whatever adheres to the vessel — that he should rinse out the vessel completely and drink in silence.

Having washed the hands, having sipped water, he lies down behind the fire — to the west of the fire — with the head turned eastward. Having worshipped the morning sandhyā, he worships the sun with the mantra "Of the directions thou art the one lotus." "Yathetam" — by the way he came; having returned, seated behind the fire, he recites the vaṃśa (the line of teachers).
BR_C06_S03_V07::block-0: This very (rite) Uddālaka Āruṇi told to his pupil Vājasaneya Yājñavalkya, and said: "Even if one should sprinkle this upon a dry stump, branches would spring forth and leaves would grow upon it."
BR_C06_S03_V08::block-0: This very (rite) Vājasaneya Yājñavalkya told to his pupil Madhuka Paiṅgya, and said: "Even if one should sprinkle this upon a dry stump, branches would spring forth and leaves would grow upon it."
BR_C06_S03_V09::block-0: Mantra: Madhuka Paiṅgya in turn imparted this very [mantha-knowledge] to his pupil Cūla Bhāgavitti, and said: "Even if one were to sprinkle this upon a dry stump, branches would grow forth and leaves would sprout." Thus the chain of teachers and the unfailing power of this rite are extolled.
BR_C06_S03_V10::block-0: Mantra: Cūla Bhāgavitti in turn imparted this very [mantha-rite] to his pupil Jānakī Āyasthūṇa and said: "Even if one were to sprinkle this upon a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves sprout forth." The arthavāda magnifies the rite by an extreme illustration.
BR_C06_S03_V11::block-0: Mantra: Jānakī Āyasthūṇa in turn imparted this very [knowledge] to his pupil Satyakāma Jābāla and said: "Even were one to sprinkle it on a dry stump, branches would arise and leaves sprout." Thus the unbroken paramparā continues.
BR_C06_S03_V12::block-0: Mantra: Satyakāma Jābāla, having imparted this very [mantha-rite] to his pupils, said: "Even if one were to sprinkle this upon a dry stump, branches would grow forth and leaves sprout." But this should not be told to one who is not a son or not a [worthy] pupil.
BR_C06_S03_V12::block-1: Bhāṣya: Beginning with "taṁ haitam Uddālakaḥ" the unbroken sequence of teachers is recapitulated. Satyakāma Jābāla, the ācārya, having transmitted to many pupils this mantha-rite which had come down by single-teacher succession from Uddālaka onwards, said further: api yaḥ enaṁ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcet — even should one pour this prepared mantha (consecrated for consumption) upon a dry stump, that is, upon wood whose vital sap (prāṇa) has departed, jāyeran eva — there would surely arise upon that very stump śākhāḥ, the limbs of a tree, prarohey- uḥ ca palāśāni, and leaves would sprout, just as upon a living stump. How much more, then, should the desired fruit be accomplished by this rite! This is arthavāda for the praise of the karman, declaring it to yield certain fruit (dhruva-phalam idaṁ karma).
BR_C06_S03_V12::block-2: Bhāṣya: For the attainment of vidyā, six tīrthas (channels of transmission) are recognised in general; but for this knowledge, namely the meditation upon the prāṇa together with the mantha-vijñāna, only two tīrthas are sanctioned — the son and the resident pupil (antevāsin). To others it is not to be communicated.
BR_C06_S03_V13::block-0: Mantra: There are four implements of audumbara wood — an audumbara sruva (ladle), an audumbara camasa (cup), audumbara firewood, and two audumbarī upamanthanīs (stirring-sticks). And there are ten village grains — rice (vrīhi), barley (yava), sesame (tila), beans (māṣa), millet (aṇu), priyaṅgu (panic-seed), wheat (godhūma), lentils (masūra), khalva (a kind of bean), and khalakula (horse-gram). These, ground into flour, he sprinkles with curds, honey and ghee, and offers oblations of clarified butter.
BR_C06_S03_V13::block-1: Bhāṣya: "Four implements of audumbara" has been already explained. "Ten village grains there are" — that is, of cultivated grains exactly ten are to be taken by rule, as we have stated. Which are they? They are now specified: vrīhi and yava, tila and māṣa, aṇu — "aṇu" being its proper name — and priyaṅgu, which in some regions is well known by the name kaṅgu (foxtail-millet); khalvāḥ, which are niṣpāva (a kind of bean), commonly called valla; khalakulāḥ, namely kulattha (horse-gram).
BR_C06_S03_V13::block-2: Bhāṣya: Apart from these, all herbs and fruits available are also to be employed according to capacity, as we have already said, with the exclusion of those that are unfit for sacrificial use (ayājñikāni).
BR_C06_S04_V01::block-0: Mantra: Of these beings the essence (rasa) is the earth; of the earth the essence is water; of waters the essence is the herbs; of herbs the essence is the flowers; of flowers the essence is the fruits; of fruits the essence is man (puruṣa); of man the essence is semen (retas).
BR_C06_S04_V01::block-1: Bhāṣya: The brāhmaṇa now beginning seeks to teach how the son, of what kind of birth, by what mode of begetting, and endowed with what qualities, becomes profitable to the self of the father and a means to a desired loka. He who has practised the prāṇa-darśana and performed the Śrīmantha-karman alone is qualified for the Putramantha. When he wishes to perform the Putramantha, he first performs the Śrīmantha and then awaits the ṛtu-kāla of his wife — this much is implied. The pre-eminent rasa-character of semen, surpassing the herbs and the rest, is conveyed by way of stuti (eulogy).
BR_C06_S04_V01::block-2: Bhāṣya: "Of these beings" — that is, of all the moving and unmoving beings — pṛthivī rasaḥ, the earth is the essence, the very substance, for it has been said elsewhere that the earth is the madhu of all beings (cf. Madhu-brāhmaṇa). Of the earth water is the essence, for the earth is woven and interwoven (otā ca protā ca) in the waters. Of waters the herbs are the rasa, since herbs are the products (kārya) of water — and rasatva belongs to that which is effect. Of herbs, the flowers; of flowers, the fruits; of fruits, the puruṣa; of the puruṣa, the retas — for another śruti declares: "From all the limbs the tejas comes together [and forms semen]" (Aitareya-Up. 2.1.1).
BR_C06_S04_V02::block-0: Mantra: Prajāpati reflected: "Come, let me devise a fitting receptacle (pratiṣṭhā) for it." He then created woman. Having created her, he worshipped her below; therefore one should worship woman below. He extended forwards out of his own self this stone (grāvan), and with that he united with her.
BR_C06_S04_V02::block-1: Bhāṣya: Since the retas is thus the supreme essence (sāratamam) of all beings, what then might be its fitting receptacle? Thus did the Creator Prajāpati reflect (īkṣāñcakre). Having so reflected, he created woman. Having created her, he "worshipped her below" (adha upāsta) — that is, he performed the act called maithuna, here named "adha-upāsana" (lower worship). Therefore one should worship woman below — for offspring follow the lead of the eminent (śreṣṭhānuśrayaṇā hi prajāḥ).
BR_C06_S04_V02::block-2: Bhāṣya: Here he establishes a similitude with the Vājapeya. "Sa enaṁ prāñcaṁ" — extending forwards, that is, of pre-eminent forward motion, the grāvan from his own self — that organ of generation which corresponds to the soma-pressing stone (somābhiṣava-upala) by virtue of common hardness (kāṭhinya-sāmānya); udapārayat — he extended fully out, towards the female organ; tena enām abhyasṛjat — by that he effected union (abhi-saṁsarga) with her.
BR_C06_S04_V03::block-0: Mantra: Her lap is the vedi (sacrificial altar); her hairs are the barhis (sacred grass); her skin is the two pressing-boards (adhiṣavaṇe); the kindled fire is in the middle; the two muṣkau (testicles) are the two soma-pressing fruits. As great as is the loka of one who performs the Vājapeya sacrifice, so great is the loka of him who, knowing thus, practises the adhopahāsa (sexual intercourse): he wrests away the merits (sukṛta) of those women. But he who, not knowing this, practises the adhopahāsa — his merits, on the contrary, the women wrest away.
BR_C06_S04_V03::block-1: Bhāṣya: "Her lap is the vedi" and the rest is all of well-known general meaning. The kindled fire (samiddho'gniḥ) is in the middle, that is, in the midst of the female organ; "the two muṣkau" are connected, by the intervening words, with the two pressing-fruits (adhiṣavaṇa-phalake). As great as is the well-known loka of the Vājapeya-sacrificer, so great is, by way of fruit, the loka of the maithuna-karman of the man who knows thus — by this stuti it is extolled. Hence one should not have aversion (bībhatsā) towards it.
BR_C06_S04_V03::block-2: Bhāṣya: "He who, knowing thus, practises the adhopahāsa, wrests away (vṛṅkte, āvarjayati) the sukṛta of those women." But on the other hand, he who is avidvān — who does not know this Vājapeya-sampatti and the rasatama-character of retas — and yet practises the adhopahāsa: of him, the avidvān, his women on the contrary wrest away (āvṛñjate) his sukṛta. Thus the contrast between the vidvān and the avidvān, and the praise of upāsanā joined to the act, is established.
BR_C06_S04_V04::block-0:
Uddālaka Āruṇi, knowing this, declared it; so too Nāka Maudgalya, knowing this, declared it; and Kumārahārita, knowing this, also declared it — namely, that the act of intercourse, called adhopahāsa, is to be performed as an offering accompanied with the vājapeya-like majesty of right understanding. The meaning is: the one who knows is one who has mastered this rite as a sacrificial act, equivalent in dignity to the vājapeya-yajña.

What then did these knowers declare? It is said: many mortals (maryāḥ, those subject to death), brāhmaṇāyanāḥ — those whose only refuge (ayana) is the mere name of brāhmaṇa, that is, brahma-bandhus who live merely on the strength of birth-caste — depart from this world devoid of the indriyas (nirindriyāḥ, with sense-organs disjoined and powerless) and stripped of merit (visukṛtaḥ, those whose puṇya-karma has departed); they are the avidvāṃsaḥ, the unknowing ones who are merely attached to the act of copulation. They depart from this very world, fallen also from the next world.

The text shows that the act of intercourse, when undertaken without knowledge, is a cause of grave demerit — "those who, being unknowing, here engage in adhopahāsa." Having performed the śrīmantha rite, one waits with brahmacarya for the wife's ṛtukāla. If, in this period, the semen is shed — be it much or little, whether one is asleep or awake — owing to the predominance of rāga (passion), the following expiatory rite is enjoined.
BR_C06_S04_V05::block-0: He should touch it (the shed semen), or recite the mantra over it — anumantrayeta means "should mutter the mantra following." When he touches it, he takes up that semen with the ring-finger and the thumb (anāmikā-aṅguṣṭhābhyām), reciting the mantra ending in "ādade" ("I take up"). Then with the next portion of the mantra beginning "punar mām" ("may it return to me"), he should wipe it (nimṛjyāt) between the two — that is, in the middle, either between the eyebrows (bhruvoḥ) or between the breasts (stanayoḥ).
BR_C06_S04_V06::block-0: Now, if at any time he should see his own image (ātmacchāyā) in water, there too he should recite this mantra — "In me be tejas (radiance)" and so forth. The wife is verily the embodiment of Śrī among women: yat — because — she is malodvāsāḥ, one whose menstrual impurity has departed (udgata-mala-vad-vāsāḥ, having a garment from which the impurity has gone forth). Therefore, having approached (abhikramya, abhigatya) that wife who has cast off the mala-stained garment, who is now yaśasvinī and śrīmatī, he should make this proposal to her: "Today the act for begetting offspring is to be done by us both" — when she has bathed at the conclusion of the three nights of her ṛtu.
BR_C06_S04_V07::block-0: If she does not consent to him for the act of intercourse, let him at will buy her over (avakrīṇīyāt) — that is, persuade her by means of ornaments and the like. Even so, if she still does not consent, then at will, having struck her with a rod or with the hand, he should overcome her (atikrāmet) for the sake of intercourse. Having declared, "I shall curse you, I shall make you ill-fortuned (durbhagā)," he should approach her with this mantra: "With my indriya, with my yaśas, I take away your yaśas" (indriyeṇa te yaśasā yaśa ādade). She, in consequence of that abhiśāpa, becomes known as barren and ill-fortuned (vandhyā durbhagā), one wholly devoid of yaśas (ayaśāḥ).
BR_C06_S04_V08::block-0: If, on the other hand, she does consent to him — that is, if she is favourable and obedient (anuguṇā) to her husband — then he should approach her with this mantra: "With my indriya, with my yaśas, I bestow yaśas upon you" (indriyeṇa te yaśasā yaśa ādadhāmi). In that case, both of them become possessed of yaśas (yaśasvinau).
BR_C06_S04_V09::block-0: Whatever woman — that is, his own wife — he should desire, thinking, "Let her too desire me," in her he places the artha, namely the prajanana-indriya (the generative organ), having deposited it (nikṣipya); having joined mouth to mouth and stroked her upastha (pudendum), he should repeat in japa this mantra — "From every aṅga (limb) thou art born, from the heart thou arisest; thou indeed art the essence drawn from the limbs (aṅga-kaṣāyaḥ); like an arrow smeared with poison (digdha-viddham), so do thou intoxicate her, this woman, towards me."
BR_C06_S04_V10::block-0: Now, if he should desire of any woman, "Let her not conceive — let her not become garbhiṇī," then in her he places the artha as before. He should first perform abhiprāṇana (in-breathing), and afterwards apānana (out-breathing) — that is, exhale — reciting this mantra: "With my indriya, with my retas, I take back the retas from you" (indriyeṇa te retasā reta ādade). She thereby becomes aretāḥ — one not bearing semen, that is, she does not become pregnant. Such is the meaning.
BR_C06_S04_V11::block-0: Now, if he should desire, "Let her conceive — let her bear the garbha," then in her he places the artha and the rest as before. By the reverse of the previous order, he should first do apānana and then abhiprāṇana, reciting: "With my indriya, with my retas, I bestow retas upon you" (indriyeṇa te retasā reta ādadhāmi). She thereby indeed becomes garbhiṇī (pregnant).
BR_C06_S04_V12::block-0: Now then, if some man's wife should have a paramour (jāra, secret lover), and the husband should hate him — should think, 'I shall practise abhicāra (hostile rite) against him' — for him this rite is prescribed. Having set up the fire in an unbaked clay pot (āma-pātra), let him perform every action in the reverse order (pratiloma); upon that fire let him offer these reed-arrows (śara-bhṛṣṭi, the sharp tips of śara reeds) reversed and smeared with ghee (sarpiṣā aktāḥ), reciting the oblations beginning 'In my kindled fire I have burnt up; thy prāṇas and apānas I take away — N. by name (asau iti),' and so forth. At the end of all the formulas the name of that paramour is to be uttered each time with 'asau iti' (so-and-so). That very man, the one whom such a knower-of-this brāhmaṇa curses, departs from this world visukṛta — that is, his stock of puṇya-karman utterly gone (vigata-puṇya-karmā). Therefore one who knows thus should not desire even sportive jest (upahāsa) with the wife of a śrotriya (one learned in the Veda) — should not even play in jest, much less indulge in adhopahāsa (sexual dalliance); for (hi) even one who merely knows thus becomes paro bhavati — that is, becomes an enemy (śatru) capable of working such ruin: this is the meaning.
BR_C06_S04_V13::block-0: Now of him whose wife should attain ārtava (the menstrual season, ṛtu-bhāva) — this passage of text, beginning 'atha yasya jāyām ārtavam vindet,' is by the force of the meaning (sāmarthyāt) to be read before the passage 'śrīr ha vā eṣā strīṇām' rather than where it stands. For three days she should drink (only) from a metal cup (kaṃsena), and should be clad in unwashed garments (ahata-vāsāḥ); during these three days neither a vṛṣala (one of low birth, bathed or unbathed) nor a vṛṣalī shall touch her — must not come into contact with her. At the end of the three nights — when the trirātra-vrata is concluded — she should bathe (āplutya, snātvā) and be clad in fresh, unwashed garments: this is the connection of the words taken with the intervening clause supplied. Then, she who has so bathed should be employed for husking the rice-grains (vrīhi) — that very wife should be assigned to the avaghāta (pounding) of the vrīhi for the rite that follows.
BR_C06_S04_V14::block-0: Now he who should desire — 'May my son be born śukla (fair-complexioned, white in varṇa); may he recite one Veda (vedam ekam anubrūyāt); may he attain the full span of life (sarvam āyuḥ iyāt) — that is, a hundred years' — let him have milk-rice (kṣīraudana) cooked, and let the two — husband and wife — eat of it together with ghee (sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām); they thereby become īśvarau, capable (samarthau), to beget — janayitavai means 'in order to beget.'
BR_C06_S04_V15::block-0: Dadhyodana means a caru (oblation-pap) cooked with curds (dadhnā) — let them have it cooked thus. If he should desire a son who would master two Vedas (dvi-vedam), then this rule of food (aśana-niyama) is to be observed.
BR_C06_S04_V16::block-0: Here is meant simply the natural, plain rice (kevalam svābhāvikam odanam — udaudana, rice cooked with water alone). The use of the word 'ud-' (in udaudana) is to exclude any other ingredient — for the nivṛtti (turning away, exclusion) of the application of anything else.
BR_C06_S04_V17::block-0: The 'paṇḍitya' (learning) of a daughter is only with regard to the management of the household (gṛha-tantra-viṣaya); for she has no adhikāra (eligibility) in the Veda. Tilaudana means kṛśara — that is, rice cooked together with sesame (and pulse).
BR_C06_S04_V18::block-0: Vigītaḥ — sung-of variously, that is, prakhyātaḥ (renowned, celebrated). Samitiṅ-gamaḥ — 'one who goes to the assembly,' meaning pragalbhaḥ (bold, eloquent in council); the word is taken in this sense, since 'paṇḍita' has been mentioned separately. Śuśrūṣitām — to be desired to be heard, agreeable, charming; bhāṣitā — speaker — that is, one who speaks saṃskṛtā (refined, well-formed) and arthavatī (full of meaning) speech: this is the meaning. Māṃsa-mixed rice is māṃsaudana. To restrict the kind of flesh, the text adds: aukṣeṇa vā — with the flesh of an ukṣan, or ārṣabheṇa — with that of an ṛṣabha. Ukṣan is a young bull capable of impregnation (sechana-samartha); the flesh derived from him is aukṣa. Ṛṣabha is one yet older than that; the flesh derived from him is ārṣabha.
BR_C06_S04_V19::block-0: Now, abhi-prātar eva — at the very early dawn — having taken the rice-grains husked (avaghāta-nirvṛttān taṇḍulān), and having performed the āja-saṃskāra (consecration of the clarified butter) according to the sthālīpāka-vidhi (the procedure for the sthālīpāka-rite), he cooks the caru and offers oblations of the sthālīpāka, scooping out (upaghātam — upahatya upahatya) at each oblation, with the formulas 'agnaye svāhā,' and so on. The whole gārhya (domestic) procedure is to be supplied here. Having thus offered, having taken out (uddhṛtya) the remainder of the caru, he himself eats (prāśnāti) of it; having eaten, he gives the leavings (ucchiṣṭam) to the wife (itarasyai). Having washed his hands (prakṣālya pāṇī) — that is, performed ācamana — and having filled the water-vessel (udapātra), with that water he sprinkles her thrice (trir abhyukṣati) with the mantra 'ut-tiṣṭhātaḥ' — the mantra being recited only once (sakṛn-mantroccāraṇam).
BR_C06_S04_V20::block-0: Mantra: "Then he approaches her: 'I am amaḥ (the vital force/strength), thou art sā (speech); thou art sā, I am amaḥ; I am the Sāman, thou art the Ṛk; I am heaven, thou art earth. Come, let us two embrace; let us mingle our seed for begetting a male child, for offspring, for wealth.'"
BR_C06_S04_V20::block-1: Bhāṣya: Now, having consecrated her with this mantra and having (first) eaten milk-rice (kṣīraudana) and the like according to the desire for a particular kind of offspring — this is the order to be observed. At the time of union, he approaches her with the mantra beginning 'amo'ham asmi' (I am amaḥ).
BR_C06_S04_V20::block-2: The procedure is thus: the husband first partakes of the prescribed food (kṣīraudana etc.) suited to the type of progeny desired (yathāpatya-kāmam); then, at the moment of saṃveśana (lying together), he formally approaches the wife reciting this mantra of identification with the cosmic pair — Sāman and Ṛk, dyaus and pṛthivī — whereby the act is consecrated as a yajña.
BR_C06_S04_V21::block-0: Mantra: "Then he parts her thighs, saying, 'Spread apart, O heaven and earth.' Having placed his organ in her, having joined mouth to mouth, he strokes her thrice along the grain of her hair (anuloma), saying: 'May Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ shape the forms; may Prajāpati pour in; may Dhātṛ bear the embryo for thee. Bear the embryo, O Sinīvālī; bear the embryo, O thou of broad braid (Pṛthuṣṭukā). May the two Aśvins, the gods garlanded with lotuses, place the embryo in thee.'"
BR_C06_S04_V21::block-1: Bhāṣya: Then he parts her thighs (vihāpayati) by uttering 'vijihīthāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī' (spread apart, O heaven and earth). 'Tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya' (having placed his organ in her) and what follows is as before. Three times he strokes her — from the head downwards in the direction of the hair (anuloma) — repeating each successive mantra beginning 'viṣṇur yonim' for each stroke (pratimantram).
BR_C06_S04_V21::block-2: The performer thus invokes the cosmic deities — Viṣṇu, Tvaṣṭṛ, Prajāpati, Dhātṛ, Sinīvālī, Pṛthuṣṭukā, and the Aśvins — each presiding over a phase of conception and embryonic formation; the threefold anuloma stroking, with one mantra per stroke (prati-mantram), accomplishes the saṃskāra of garbhādhāna by uniting the human act with divine sanction.
BR_C06_S04_V22::block-0: Mantra: "'The two golden kindling-sticks (araṇī) by which the Aśvins churn — that embryo of thine we invoke, that thou mayest be delivered in the tenth month. As earth bears Agni in her womb, as heaven is pregnant with Indra, as wind is the embryo of the quarters, even so do I place an embryo in thee, O so-and-so.'"
BR_C06_S04_V22::block-1: Bhāṣya: At the end he pronounces her name — 'asau' (so-and-so) — that is, hers (the wife's actual name).
BR_C06_S04_V22::block-2: Here the formula 'asau' is the placeholder; the officiant must utter the wife's proper name in its place, thereby individualizing the otherwise general mantra and binding the saṃskāra to the specific person upon whom the rite is performed.
BR_C06_S04_V23::block-0: Mantra: "He sprinkles her with water when she is about to give birth: 'As the wind shakes a lotus-pond on every side, so let thy embryo stir and come forth together with the placenta. This is Indra's enclosure, fitted with a bolt and barrier; O Indra, expel it forth — the embryo together with the afterbirth.'"
BR_C06_S04_V23::block-1: Bhāṣya: When she is about to give birth (soṣyantī), he sprinkles her with water (adbhir abhyukṣati) at the time of delivery, for the sake of an easy delivery (sukha-prasavana), with this very mantra — 'yathā vāyuḥ puṣkariṇīṃ samiṅgayati sarvataḥ; evā te garbha ejatu' (As the wind agitates a lotus-pond on every side, so let thy embryo stir).
BR_C06_S04_V23::block-2: The simile of wind moving the waters of a lotus-pond conveys the desired ease and natural unforced motion of parturition; the sprinkling with water (abhyukṣaṇa) is the prayoga, the actual ritual application accompanying the recitation, both together constituting the means for sukha-prasava.
BR_C06_S04_V24::block-0: Mantra: "When the child is born, having set up the fire, having taken him on his lap, having mixed pṛṣadājya (curds-and-ghee) in a metal cup, he offers oblations of pṛṣadājya: 'In him may I prosper a thousandfold, increasing in my own house — svāhā. May his livelihood not be cut off — together with offspring and cattle — svāhā. In me I offer the prāṇas, in thee with mind I offer — svāhā. Whatever in this rite I have done excessively, or whatever I have here done deficiently — may Agni, the All-knowing Sviṣṭakṛt, make it well-offered, well-sacrificed for us — svāhā.'"
BR_C06_S04_V24::block-1: Bhāṣya: Now, the jātakarman (birth-saṃskāra). When the child is born (jāte), having set up the fire (agnim upasamādhāya), having placed the son on his lap (aṅke ādhāya), having mixed (sannīya = saṃyojya) pṛṣadājya in a metal cup (kaṃse) — that is, having combined it with curds and ghee (dadhi-ghṛte) — he offers an oblation (upaghātam juhoti) of the pṛṣadājya at the place of avāpa (insertion of the libation), with the formulae 'asmin sahasram' and the rest.
BR_C06_S04_V24::block-2: The compound pṛṣadājya is etymologized as ājya (clarified butter) mixed with curds (dadhi) — Śaṅkara explains saṃnīya by sannīya = saṃyojya (having joined together); the upaghāta is the partial dipping or insertion at the prescribed place (āvāpa-sthāna), each mantra accompanied by its own offering, and the rite as a whole effects the jātakarman saṃskāra of the newborn.
BR_C06_S04_V25::block-0: Mantra: "Then placing his mouth close to the child's right ear, he says thrice 'vāk, vāk' (speech, speech). Then having mixed curds, honey, and ghee, with gold (jātarūpa) not separated (anantarhita), he makes him taste — saying: 'Bhūr I place in thee, Bhuvas I place in thee, Svar I place in thee; Bhūr-Bhuvas-Svar — the All — I place in thee.'"
BR_C06_S04_V25::block-1: Bhāṣya: Then placing his own mouth close to the child's right ear, he should mutter thrice 'vāg vāk' (speech, speech). Then having mixed curds, honey, and ghee (sannīya = combined), with anantarhita — that is, unseparated (avyavahita), without anything intervening — gold (jātarūpa = hiraṇya), he feeds (prāśayati) him with these mantras, one for each (pratyekam).
BR_C06_S04_V25::block-2: Anantarhita is glossed as avyavahita: the gold must touch the mixture directly, with no intervening medium (such as a leaf or cloth) between the metal and the food; jātarūpa is etymologized as hiraṇya (gold) — that which has 'jāta-rūpa', the natural-born form. The threefold whispering of 'vāk' invokes the goddess Speech into the right ear, and the prāśana (feeding) accompanied by the Bhūr-Bhuvas-Svar formulae invests the child with the threefold worlds, each mantra correlated with its own act of tasting (prati-mantram).
BR_C06_S04_V25::block-3: Thus through ear, mouth, and the medium of consecrated food, the saṃskāra of medhājanana (generation of intelligence) is performed; the gold imparts purity and longevity, while the vyāhṛtis confer the totality of the universe upon the newborn.
BR_C06_S04_V26::block-0: Mantra: "Then he gives him a name, saying 'Veda art thou' — that becomes his secret name (guhya-nāma)."
BR_C06_S04_V26::block-1: Bhāṣya: Then he confers a name (nāmadheya) upon him, saying 'vedo'si' (Veda art thou). That becomes his secret name (guhya-nāma) — namely, 'Veda'.
BR_C06_S04_V26::block-2: There are two names of the child: the public, customary name (vyāvahārika) used in worldly transactions, and the secret name (guhya-nāma) — here 'Veda' — known only to the parents and used for ritual purposes; the latter, by its very meaning, identifies the son with sacred knowledge itself.
BR_C06_S04_V27::block-0: Mantra: "Then having handed him over to the mother, he gives him the breast, saying: 'That breast of thine which is ever-flowing, refreshing, the giver of treasure, finder of wealth, generous in bestowing — by which thou nourishest all desirable things, O Sarasvatī — that, here, give him to suck.'"
BR_C06_S04_V27::block-1: Bhāṣya: Then having handed him — who was on his own lap (svāṅka-stham) — over to the mother, he gives him the breast (stanaṃ prayacchati) with the mantra beginning 'yas te stanaḥ' (that breast of thine).
BR_C06_S04_V27::block-2: The transfer from the father's lap (sva-aṅka-stha) to the mother marks the conclusion of the father's portion of the jātakarman; the breast is then offered with invocation of Sarasvatī, identifying the mother's milk with the divine nourishment that 'finds wealth' (vasuvit) and 'gives treasure' (ratnadhā), so that the saṃskāra of stanya-prāśana too is consecrated.
BR_C06_S04_V28::block-0: Then he addresses its mother with the formula "Ilā art thou" — "Ilā art thou, daughter of Mitra and Varuṇa; thou hast brought forth a hero through a hero (i.e. through me, a hero, thou hast given birth to a hero); mayest thou too be the mother of heroes, thou who hast made us possessed of a hero." Of him, the son so begotten, they say: "Verily thou hast surpassed thy father, verily thou hast surpassed thy grandfather; verily he hath attained the highest pinnacle (paramāṁ kāṣṭhām) by śrī (prosperity), yaśas (fame) and brahmavarcasa (the radiance of brahminhood) — he who is born as the son of a brāhmaṇa who knows thus."
BR_C06_S04_V28::block-1: Now he addresses its mother by the formula "Ilā art thou" (ilāsi). "They say of him" — meaning, by this prescribed procedure (vidhinā) the son who is begotten surpasses (atiśete) his father and grandfather, and in śrī, yaśas and brahmavarcasa attains the highest summit (paramāṁ niṣṭhām) — thus he becomes worthy of such praise. And of him whose father is a brāhmaṇa knowing thus, the son who is born — he too becomes worthy of such praise; this is to be supplied (adhyāhārya) in the construal.
BR_C06_S05_V01::block-0: Now the lineage (vaṁśa). The son of Pautimāṣī (received the teaching) from the son of Kātyāyanī; the son of Kātyāyanī from the son of Gautamī; the son of Gautamī from the son of Bhāradvājī; the son of Bhāradvājī from the son of Pārāśarī; the son of Pārāśarī from the son of Aupasvastī; the son of Aupasvastī from the son of Pārāśarī; the son of Pārāśarī from the son of Kātyāyanī; the son of Kātyāyanī from the son of Kauśikī; the son of Kauśikī from the son of Ālambī and the son of Vaiyāghrapadī; the son of Vaiyāghrapadī from the son of Kāṇvī and the son of Kāpī; the son of Kāpī …
BR_C06_S05_V01::block-1: Now is set forth the entire lineage of the teaching-tradition (samasta-pravacana-vaṁśa), being designated through the mother's side because of the prominence of the woman (strī-prādhānyāt). It has been declared that the son becomes endowed with virtue (guṇavān bhavati); hence by the qualification of the mother itself the qualification of the son is given, and so the succession of teachers (ācārya-paramparā) is recounted. "These are the white (śuklāni)" — that is, unmixed (avyāmiśrāṇi) with [the rituals of] the brāhmaṇa portion; or alternatively, those Yajus mantras which are these are śukla, i.e. pure (śuddha) — this is the meaning. From Prajāpati down to the son of Pautimāṣī, the lineage proceeds downward (adho-mukha) with the order of preceptors fixed (niyatācārya-pūrva-krama), and is uniform up to the son of Sāñjīvī. [It comes from] Brahman, named the prime utterance (pravacana-ākhya); and this very Brahman, having come down through the unbroken series beginning with Prajāpati, has spread among us in many ways — the beginningless, endless, self-existent, eternal Brahman. To that Brahman be salutation; salutation also to the gurus who follow it.
BR_C06_S05_V02::block-0: [The son of Kāpī received the teaching] from the son of Ātreyī; the son of Ātreyī from the son of Gautamī; the son of Gautamī from the son of Bhāradvājī; the son of Bhāradvājī from the son of Pārāśarī; the son of Pārāśarī from the son of Vātsī; the son of Vātsī from the son of Pārāśarī; the son of Pārāśarī from the son of Vārkāruṇī; the son of Vārkāruṇī from the son of Vārkāruṇī; the son of Vārkāruṇī from the son of Ārtabhāgī; the son of Ārtabhāgī from the son of Śauṅgī; the son of Śauṅgī from the son of Sāṅkṛtī; the son of Sāṅkṛtī from the son of Ālambāyanī; the son of Ālambāyanī from the son of Ālambī; the son of Ālambī from the son of Jāyantī; the son of Jāyantī from the son of Māṇḍūkāyanī; the son of Māṇḍūkāyanī from the son of Māṇḍūkī; the son of Māṇḍūkī from the son of Śāṇḍalī; the son of Śāṇḍalī from the son of Rāthītarī; the son of Rāthītarī from the son of Bhālukī; the son of Bhālukī from the two sons of Krauñcikī; the two sons of Krauñcikī from the son of Vaidabhṛtī; the son of Vaidabhṛtī from the son of Kārśakeyī; the son of Kārśakeyī from the son of Prācīnayogī; the son of Prācīnayogī from the son of Sāñjīvī; the son of Sāñjīvī from Prāśnīputra Āsurivāsin; Prāśnīputra from Āsurāyaṇa; Āsurāyaṇa from Āsuri; Āsuri from [the next teacher].
BR_C06_S05_V03::block-0: [Āsuri received] from Yājñavalkya; Yājñavalkya from Uddālaka; Uddālaka from Aruṇa; Aruṇa from Upaveśi; Upaveśi from Kuśri; Kuśri from Vājaśravas; Vājaśravas from Jihvāvat Bādhyoga; Jihvāvat Bādhyoga from Asita Vārṣagaṇa; Asita Vārṣagaṇa from Harita Kāśyapa; Harita Kāśyapa from Śilpa Kāśyapa; Śilpa Kāśyapa from Kāśyapa Naidhruvi; Kāśyapa Naidhruvi from Vāc; Vāc from Ambhiṇī; Ambhiṇī from Āditya. These white Yajus mantras (śuklāni yajūṁṣi), received from Āditya, are proclaimed by Yājñavalkya of the Vājasaneya line.
BR_C06_S05_V04::block-0: Up to the son of Sāñjīvī the lineage is the same (samānam ā sāñjīvīputrāt). The son of Sāñjīvī (received) from Māṇḍūkāyani; Māṇḍūkāyani from Māṇḍavya; Māṇḍavya from Kautsa; Kautsa from Māhitthi; Māhitthi from Vāmakakṣāyaṇa; Vāmakakṣāyaṇa from Śāṇḍilya; Śāṇḍilya from Vātsya; Vātsya from Kuśri; Kuśri from Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana; Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana from Tura Kāvaṣeya; Tura Kāvaṣeya from Prajāpati; Prajāpati from Brahman. Brahman is self-existent (svayambhū). To that Brahman be salutation.
